title: Weeping and joy: the not-understanding that reaches the Essence
overview:
The chapter opens with the saying "weeping is lodged in my heart on one side, and joy on the other": the soul becomes a ready vessel for G-dliness only when both come together. Then the question: joy is born of comprehension, in *bina*, yet comprehension never catches Him; *chachma*, which is *ayin*, should have the joy, but its *bittul* is the opposite of joy.

The answer is that everything has its opposite, one power in two equal lines. The power of *bina* is the power of not understanding, and the Essence, beyond understanding, is what it is really after. So the weeping comes in three levels: over the explanation not yet understood, over the *hafla'a* of *chachma*, and over the Essence that can never fit in the mind. That felt emptiness is the vessel. The comprehension is of a *tzimtzum*, but the joy reaches the Essence: now through the weeping of exile, in the future as laughter. The tears of *tikkun chatzos* prepare the way; in our days the Rebbe goes straight to the joy, but *Chassidus* that does not make a man more observant is not *Chassidus*. And this explanation, Rabbi Markel says, is the *tevuna* of the Essence.

sections.title: Weeping on one side and joy on the other: the preparation of the soul
sections.summary: Before the soul can take in the knowledge of G-dliness it has to be made a ready vessel, and that is done only by weeping and joy together, two opposites from one contemplation. One without the other, or both only on the surface, is a sure sign that nothing went in.

phrases.en: From one side is crying, from one side is happiness.

blocks.text: Chapter 6 is in a way a continuation of chapter 5. It is not about *chachma* (wisdom) and *bina* (understanding) as such: within each of them there is *bechiya* (weeping) and *chedva* (joy). It opens with the saying *bechiya tekiya b'libai mi'sitra da v'chedva mi'sitra da*: from one side crying, from one side happiness.

blocks.text: There has to be this *hachana* (preparation). Which means that if you do not have this *hachana*, you are not a *kli muchan* (a ready vessel).

In our days, according to what the Rebbe says, we can do this *lechatchila ariber* (going over the top from the start): start studying, and the *hachana* will come on its own. That is so in general, and even in *avodas hamochin* (the service of the mind).

sections.title: The question: joy is in bina, and comprehension does not reach Him
sections.summary: Delight is in *chachma* and joy in *bina*, born of comprehension; yet the main joy is in G-dliness itself, and comprehension never catches Him. So the joy should be in *chachma*, which is *ayin*; but *chachma* is *bittul*, the opposite of joy.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים הנה ידוע דענג ושמחה הוא בחכמה ובינה,
הענג בחכמה ושמחה בבינה
(וזהו ההפרש בין שבת ליום טוב כידוע)
כי ההשגה בשכל מוליד השמחה
שהוא שמחת הנפש
כמו שכתוב אם הבנים שמחה

blocks.text: The difference between *Shabbos* and *Yom Tov* is that *Shabbos* is *oneg* (delight), as it says *oneg Shabbos*, and *Yom Tov* is *v'samachta b'chagecha*. It is like what was said before: *em habanim semeicha*.

phrases.he: וידוע שעיקר השמחה דווקא באלהו״ת הוא,
phrases.en: the main thing of the *simcha* is *davka* in the *Elokus*

phrases.he: וכמו וישמחו בך דוקא
phrases.en: they will be happy *davka* by You

blocks.text: The main joy is *davka* in G-dliness, not in the explanation; joy in the explanation is not the real joy: they will rejoice *davka* in You. Which is very strange. How is that possible? The joy of *bina* is into the *musag*, the thing grasped; *bina* stops at the explanation and does not get to the *etzem hadavar* (the thing itself). But it makes no difference.

blocks.title: The Steelers won
blocks.text: The joy comes from the thing itself, even when you only hear about it. You hear on the radio that the Steelers won: "then he ran, and he went to the 10th, and he went to the 5th..." You are hearing it from far away, but what makes you happy is not the explanation; it is that the guy made the goal. So here: we hear only an explanation, but the joy comes from the thing itself, the actual G-dliness.

Not only that: even though *bina* is into an explanation, its *ratzon* (will), the *Keser* (crown) of *bina*, is *davka* to understand the actual thing. That is one reason *bina* has no upper limit and no lower limit. None of the *middos* (attributes) really has one, but in a way they do; *bina* does not. It can go without limit, up and down, in a way of a *yesh*.

You see it going down: *bina* goes into the physical reality in a way of a *yesh*, until we actually have cars and computers. *Chachma*, a thing of *ayin* (nothing), will not necessarily give you a way to make actual *yesh* things in the physical reality. *Bina* does.

blocks.title: The scientific method is iyun
blocks.text: People think science is a philosophy. It is really a methodology, and that methodology is *iyun* (close analysis). You make a theory, a *sevara* (a line of reasoning), and test it, just as in the Talmud: "Maybe it's like this. So how would that apply to that thing?" "Wait, it seems to work." Then another guy says, "No, look at this," and he blows up your *sevara*. In science you test the theory against the actual facts of reality; a scientific experiment is a set of things built to make that test. The whole scientific method is a thing of *iyun*.

The scientific theory is one of the expressions of the eighth king of *Tohu* (the world of Chaos): a *bina* of *Tohu*, unconnected to G-d. Yet the eighth king does not die. The scientists started off in the 19th century "very full of themselves", sure they had disproved that there is a G-d; the more they get into it, the more they see that there seems to be a Controller of the universe.

blocks.text: *Bina* is into the actual thing, as you see in the physical world. And here too: we are hearing a bunch of explanations, but we are not even really trying to understand how the world came into being; that too is a *mashal* (analogy). What we are really trying to understand is what G-d is, and what we are doing here. That is what *Chassidus* is about.

But *v'yismechu becha* is in the *Aibershter* (the One Above, G-d) *mamash*. Our joy in learning is not because it is an intricate, detailed study, or because we get to understand psychology. "I could come up with more intricate, detailed studies": we could study quantum mechanics, and "I wouldn't get a *simcha*; as a matter of fact, I would get bored."

blocks.text: A joy in what? Not in the intricate study, the talking and discussing. People have philosophy groups: they get together and *hak a tchainik* (Yiddish: bang a kettle, chatter on). They even have a politics group that discusses communism, though they're all Republicans, and get a big joy and *taanug* out of the intricacies of the explanations. The joy of that *bina* comes from the beauty of the explanation. That is not what is happening here.

blocks.title: An explanation is an elegant building
blocks.text: An explanation is a *binyan*, a building, an elegant structure. Some people do mathematical problems not to reach a solution, but because they love going through the elegant structures of mathematics. The ancient Arabs and Greeks who came up with algebra got their joy and *taanug* from the elegance of the structure itself; it was not so much a matter of *bina*. The joy of *Chassidus*, he is telling you, does not come from the elegance of the structure. It comes from the G-dliness, because that is the actual subject.

blocks.question: Is "they will rejoice in You" a positive comprehension of what the *Aibershter* is, the thing we try to make contact with?
blocks.text: Not contact: it is what we are trying to understand, in a way of a *yesh*. Right now it is not an actual comprehension, but later he will promise *nagila v'nismecha becha mamash*: when *Moshiach* comes, we will have it.

blocks.text: Why is *bina* into the *etzem* (essence) of the thing? Because it has the power to grasp the *etzem*, *davka* being the *yesh*, and it is connected to all its levels: up and up and up, down and down and down. So the intellect going down into the physical world catches it, until it is not just a theory of a car anymore: you can actually make a car, a combustion engine and a wheel put together.

blocks.text: *Bina* is grasping. ("Comprehension?" "Not comprehension, grasping. To hold on to the thing.") In Hebrew, *litfos*: as he says elsewhere, he thinks in chapter one, the *ba'al bina* is called a *tafsan* (a grasper). He takes hold of the actual *etzem*, so that the *bina* of the physical world grasps the thing and you can make actual changes in physical things.

blocks.title: "I don't understand my children"
blocks.text: Architecture, or the engineering of a car, aerodynamics, is just intellectual; yet he does not want only the theory of aerodynamics: he wants to understand how the physical world actually works. Somebody says, "I don't understand my children": he wants to understand them to the point where he can make a change in them, actually control their behavior ("I don't mean control necessarily in a bad way"), affect it. Or, "I would like to understand politics." Some people are interested only in the *bina* itself, not the *etzem* of the thing. That is not the real *inyan* of *bina*: it is to understand the thing itself.

phrases.he: ולפי הנזכר לעיל דבהשגה לית מחשבה תפיסא ביה,
phrases.en: according to what we said in the last chapter, that *machshava* of *bina* actually does not catch Him

phrases.he: אדרבה מופלא
phrases.en: the thing is totally separated, a totally wondrous thing

phrases.he: בהפלאת הערך הנבדל כו'
phrases.en: not just that it's wondrous according to our *erech*, but it's totally non-comparative to anything we can think of

phrases.he: והיינו בבחינת כח מ''ה דחכמה בהעלם כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: and this is *davka* in the *koach MaH* of the *chachma* that sees

blocks.text: But according to the last chapter, the thought of *bina* does not catch Him at all. He is totally separate, wondrous, so that you see it makes no sense at all; and not wondrous by our measure only, but beyond compare, non-comparable to anything we can think of.

This is *davka* in the *koach MaH* of *chachma* (the power of *chachma* that sees what a thing is). It is not only that *bina* itself shows you some details are missing. From the power of *chachma* you actually see that there is a wondrous thing, "a fantastically wondrous thing", that the *bina* is not describing. That comes from the overview of the whole: taking it in, you see that all the particulars are missing something, and not only that they miss it: you have a sight of it. You see into the actual *mahus* (what it is in itself) of the thing, and that it is totally *nivdal*, separate, from what the explanation is talking about.

Is it by way of *shlila*, negation? No. Negation is in *bina*: the comprehension of *bina* is by negation, but the sight of *chachma* is *mamash* like seeing the thing, a positive thing. It is awakened by the power of *bina*, from its negation. There is deductive logic, inductive logic, and another kind. Deductive logic says: this, therefore that. You bring up various *pratim* (particulars) and come to a conclusion: a comprehension, not of negation, of what the conclusion actually is.

blocks.title: The red ball in one of twenty pockets
blocks.text: *Hasagas hashlila* (comprehension by negation) is like this. We know that one of 20 people in the room has a red ball in his pocket. We check 19, and they don't have it. This is almost deductive logic, not a real negation, but it is the beginning: you never looked in his pocket. "Well, it must be him, because it's not them."

blocks.title: Who controls your stomach?
blocks.text: Who is controlling your stomach? Not you: sometimes it goes out of control and you can't put it back. You're all full, somebody brings a fantastic dish you love, and you can't make yourself hungry. You have nothing to do with your stomach, so it must be G-d who controls it; but you have no comprehension of how. That is *hasagas hashlila*.

blocks.title: The palace in the forest
blocks.text: In general, *hasagas hashlila* is what you are compelled to when you look around: one of the *meshalim* (analogies) they give that there must be a creator of the world. You come into a palace in the middle of the forest, with food in the refrigerator. You can't say, "I wonder how many billions of years it took till the stones fell into the shape of a palace?" "What are you talking about?" There has to be a *ba'al habayis* (an owner) to this *bira* (palace), but you don't see him. That is the first level of *hasagas hashlila*.

Another level, the real thing of *hasagas hashlila*, is that you can't figure out what the thing is, but you can figure out what it isn't. That is what the *Rambam* (Maimonides) talks about. The first is really deductive logic, this therefore that: the 20th guy has the ball only if you are told for sure that one of them has it. (The side ends here.)

You can't figure out what the *Aibershter* is, but you can figure out that He is not Jesus. He is not a person. "If you know so good, so what is it?" "The actual *mahus* you can't figure out. But I can tell you what it's not." That is the real *hasagas hashlila*: a comprehension, not in *chachma*, but an actual form of logic that figures out what the thing is not.

blocks.title: The mountain that keeps getting bigger
blocks.text: What it sees in the *mahus* is not so much what it is, just how far removed it is. You walk towards a big, big mountain: "Must be about a mile away. That's a really big mountain." You walk three miles, and it looks much bigger: "Wait a minute, it wasn't a mile away; now it looks maybe five miles away." The more you keep walking, the bigger and farther it gets.

blocks.title: The mountain that keeps getting bigger
blocks.text: Your sense of *hafla'a* (wondrousness) grows, and then it does a double take. It hits you: "I have no idea how big it is or how far away it is. That I see it at a certain size and distance is just an imagination, a mirage." That is the real *hafla'a* of the *Aibershter*: not seeing how big it is, but realizing you are making a whole mistake, and no matter how much you travel it will keep getting bigger and farther.

blocks.text: So even the *hafla'a* is not unconnected to *bina*: there is no *bina* without *chachma* and no *chachma* without *bina*. The sense of *hafla'a* comes from the *hasagas hashlila*, yet it is positive: you actually see it. *Bina* says, "Well, it's none of these things," and from this comes the *hafla'a* of *chachma*.

blocks.text: The *bittul* is actually the opposite of joy. In *bittul* you feel like you're nothing.

blocks.title: The wedding and the Cossacks
blocks.text: Joy is like when he's at a wedding, drank a bunch of booze, and he's jumping around. Joy is like a bunch of Cossacks: they feel they're something, everybody dancing and knocking everybody on the back. Whereas *bittul* is the opposite of joy, and it is in *chachma*; the joy is in *bina*. So what's going on here?

sections.title: Everything has its opposite: one power in two equal lines
sections.summary: A thing's whole power comes from its opposite, as delight and pain measure each other: one power divided into two equal lines. So the push of *bina* comes from not understanding, and its real object is the Essence, which is the most not-understandable of all.

phrases.en: now is the explanation

phrases.en: in everything there is also its opposite

blocks.text: Now the explanation: everything has its opposite in it. Though it appears to be *mamash* its total opposite, from this itself we see that its whole power comes *davka* from the opposite.

The power of understanding comes from not understanding. What pushes you to want to understand is that you don't understand something; the push to understand is to understand what you don't understand.

So he is saying not only that the *bina* of *Chassidus* is into *Elokus* (G-dliness), but that the whole thing of *bina* is *davka* into *Elokus*, because that is the most non-understandable thing. Other things could be understood; this is not just not understood, it is non-understandable. So the real push of *bina* is the *bina* into *Elokus* itself, its exact opposite.

phrases.he: ולפי ערך כח המנגד כן ימצא כח היפוכו ממש,
phrases.en: it's *davka* the power of the opposite that gives the power to the thing

phrases.he: אם כן כדבר אחד ממש הוא
phrases.en: that means that it's really *mamash* one thing

blocks.text: It is so in the *sefarim* (the books) with delight and pain, weeping and joy: as much as you miss somebody, that's how much you want him there, and how happy you'll be when he's there. The power of the opposite gives the thing its power: it is *mamash* one thing.

דהיינו אם יעמוד לנגדו דבר לבטל הענג ההוא להיות מן ההיפוך כו'
phrases.en: if something will prevent him from having this thing, that's how much *tza'ar* he's going to have, according to how much *oneg* he had

phrases.he: וכן להיפך,
ערך הענג מדבר מה לא יוכר רק לפי ערך הצער בהעדר אותו הדבר כו'

blocks.text: Like delight and pain: as much delight as he had in the thing, that is how much pain he will have if something prevents him from having it. And the reverse, exactly the same.

So it is *mamash* one power: the whole power of understanding comes from not understanding. Say, as it were, we understood this better than the Mitteler Rebbe (the author): we wouldn't read this book. We read it because we don't understand it. That's the whole thing.

You see somebody trying real hard to understand something: he's working, doing *hisbonenus*, thinking about it. What does it mean? That he doesn't understand it. So the real power of *bina*, more than of all the other *sefiros*, is *Atzmus Elokus* (the Essence of G-dliness). *Bina* is *mamash* rooted there, because that is "the totally ununderstandable thing there is", the total antithesis of *bina*.

In love or fear it is not the total antithesis. Even in *chachma* it is the opposite only to a certain extent, not like *bina*. In *bina* it is *mamash* the total opposite; so what *bina* really is, is *atzmuso umahuso*, His Essence and being, its opposite. Of all the things you can't understand, that is the most: not that you don't understand it yet, but *mamash* totally non-understandable. In *chachma* you can have a flash, an intuitive thing into *Elokus* (not that it is actually into *Elokus*), so it is still not the total opposite. But he is telling you that the Essence is *bina*.

phrases.he: הרי כח אחד הוא ממש,
phrases.en: it's *mamash* one thing

phrases.he: רק שנחלק לב' קווין שוין ממש ושקולין
phrases.en: two equal lines going in two different directions, and they weigh exactly

phrases.he: בלתי יטה כח קו א' על ב' אפילו כקוצו של יו״ד

blocks.text: So it is *mamash* one power. The Essence is the totally non-understandable, and because it is the opposite, it is the actual power of *bina*: what drives somebody to understand is that he doesn't understand.

blocks.question: When someone knows something is unattainable, doesn't he give up hope of it?
blocks.text: That is not really true; it depends how much *taanug* there is in it. A heroin addict knows he can't get that first high anymore, but he's still trying, because of the *taanug*. The pain can put him into a melancholy, *atzvus*, so that he stops. But that is the whole thing he explains: you are supposed to have *marirus* (bitterness), not *atzvus*. *Marirus* is the opposite power that *davka* drives you.

Two equal lines going in two directions weigh exactly the same. So the pain and the delight are the same, and so are the not understanding and the drive to understand. The drive to understand is strongest in *Elokus*, to the point that the actual *mahus* of *bina* is the *mahus* of the *Aibershter*.

Look very closely, and the *mahus* of *bina* into anything else, understanding your children or psychology, comes down to one thing: what you really want to understand is *Elokus*. That, of course, is why the eighth king does not die. Whatever he is trying to understand, the real thing is *davka* *Elokus*, so he can't really become disconnected. *Bina* can get hung up in the details for a while, but it doesn't matter. Even by the tip of a *yud*: not even like a dot.

sections.title: Joy and weeping in bina, and in the hidden delight of chachma
sections.summary: The more one has tasted G-dliness in comprehension, the more one weeps over its hiding, to the point of disgust with one's life; and above that, the hidden delight of *chachma* brings a *bittul* that throws away everything that feels itself. In each, the two lines weigh the same; and *bina*, which grasps nothing of the Essence, is the most opposite and so the most bound to it.

phrases.he: וכן החדווה והבכיה,
phrases.en: so the same thing with *chedva* and *bechiya*

phrases.he: שלפי ערך החדווה, שהוא ענג המורגש בגלוי אלקות בהשגתו כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: exactly according to how much he's enjoying what is his *hasaga* into the *gilui Elokus*, exactly according to that

phrases.he: כך ימצא קו הב' שיוצא ממנו ומכחו דוקא

blocks.text: So with joy and weeping: the weeping is exactly according to how much he enjoys his comprehension of G-dliness, how much he understands. The more *Chassidus* you learn, the more what you don't understand will bother you. A guy who doesn't understand nothing isn't bothered at all; a guy who knows a whole bunch of *Chassidus* will be bothered until he is *mo'es b'chayav mamash* (disgusted with his life).

They tell him, "What if we make you Bill Gates, a super zillionaire, but you'll have to give up *Chassidus*?" "There's no way, man." He can't stand the whole world: "I can't take this world. *Moshiach* has to come, so that we'll be able to sit and study the whole time," and not get tired, one giant *farbrengen* (a Chassidic gathering). As you see by the Rebbe, a *farbrengen* means you study *Chassidus*, and eat, and sleep, everything right there at the table; even the song between the *maamarim* (discourses) is part of the *Chassidus*.

מצד הסתר אלהו״ת,
עד שמואס בחייו ממש
phrases.en: till he says, "I can't take my life anymore"

blocks.text: Until he is *mo'es b'chayav mamash*: "I can't take my life anymore. Every day I have to go to work, do this and that. *Moshiach* has to come." As the *Rambam* rules: they wanted *Moshiach* not for the external things, *ma'adanim k'afar*, but because it will give them time to study *Chassidus*.

phrases.en: what do I have to do with anything in heaven, and what do I want from anything on earth? Other than You.

blocks.text: So too the *oneg hane'lam* (hidden delight) in *chachma*: he doesn't even know he's there anymore, *tzu tragen gor fun zich* (Yiddish: totally gone from himself). It is from the *oneg hane'lam* into the Essence, the flash of the *hafla'a*.
The opposite of it is that he will totally throw his life away against anything that will stop him from this. That means anything that will make him feel himself.

That is, to be totally *mo'es* in his life: *mi li vashamayim*, what do I have in heaven, *v'imcha lo chafatzti va'aretz*, what do I want on earth, other than You? Don't bother me with heaven or earth: "I want only *Chassidus*." *Kala she'eri ul'vavi*, my meat and my heart are gone: nothing to do with my emotions or my meat.

phrases.he: כי ב' קווין שקולים בשווה הן כנזכר לעיל ודי למבין.
phrases.en: 'cause it's *mamash* the same thing

blocks.text: Because the delight and the weeping are *mamash* the same thing. And in *chachma* too, the *chachma* is *davka* into the Essence, because the whole thing of *chachma* is that he feels he doesn't have it: the *hafla'a*. But the main thing is *davka* in *bina*. *Chachma* is the *ayin*, so not having it is what *chachma* is, not a total negation; only in *bina* is it a total negation.

So with *chesed* (kindness): there is a negation there, which is why the real love is *davka* into the Essence: he feels it is impossible to love G-d properly. But he can love G-d a little bit. In *bina*, with all the explanations, he feels he is not understanding G-d at all, totally. It is a total lack.

All the other things have their opposite too; that is the real *inyan* of all the *middos*. "What do you mean, *bina* comes from *Elokus* and the other *middos* don't?" They all come from *Elokus*, and He is *mikol ilein middos*, the opposite of all of them; but nothing like *bina*. That is why the whole thing is *bina sheb'bina* (*bina* within *bina*): the strongest power into *Elokus*.

blocks.text: So *bina* is a very special *sefira*, *davka* into the Essence. The lack of the thing is a *kaf shakul*, a pan of the scale weighing the same as the thing. You see the difference between *bina* and the other *sefiros* in a couple of ways. One: *davka* in *bina*, the lack of *bina* makes you want *bina*.
blocks.outOfPlace: After line 35 the class goes on as a free discussion of the chapter's point about bina; it is placed with the line it follows.

blocks.text: In the other *sefiros* it is not necessarily so. Lacking *ratzon* for something does not make you want to want it. Lacking *taanug* in something makes you, just the opposite, not want it. Lacking *chachma*, which is *bittul*, does not make you want *bittul*, and lacking love or hatred does not make you have it. The only one a little like *bina* is *netzach* (victory): if you're losing, you want to win. But only in a person who already has *netzach*: a person who is not ambitious (ambition is *netzach*) is not made ambitious by his lack of it. That is so in all the *middos*: once you have the *midda*, its lack makes you want more.
blocks.outOfPlace: After line 35 the class goes on as a free discussion of the chapter's point about bina; it is placed with the line it follows.

blocks.text: But in *bina* you see that even a stupid person, not a *bina* type... You'd say it applies here too: a non-intellectual is not trying to become an intellectual; just the opposite, he thinks they're all eggheads. But it's not true. Every person, "no matter how stupid he is", wants to be a *mevin* (one who understands). Like the kind of people around here: they'll tell you why the Steelers lost, the quarterback made that play wrong, he should have done it like that, a whole analysis. And then they feel like they're a *mevin*.

Every person wants to be a *mevin* (one who understands). Talk to any fan: he'll tell you why the Steelers lost, the quarterback made that play wrong, he should have done it like that, a whole analysis. And then he feels like he's a *mevin*.

blocks.text: Everybody has to feel he's a *mevin*; their whole ego depends on it. Football is a matter of *netzach*, but they have to show they're a *mevin*: "Well, the strategy was wrong." Any conversation, at the back of the *shul* or at the pool hall: the stock market should have been like this, the politics should have been like that, whatever they're into. Their whole ego depends *davka* on the *bina*, because *bina* is a *yesh*.

blocks.title: The snake's new names
blocks.text:
A man came to the Mitteler Rebbe and said he has a *hargashas hayesh*, a feeling of his own existence. The Rebbe asked him, "You know what *hargashas hayesh* means?" The man was smart enough to just shut up. "Let me tell you a story."

The primordial snake had a job to do. After *Adam HaRishon* realized what had happened, the snake came crying to the *Aibershter*: "Nobody's going to listen to me. They're scared of a snake." "Don't worry, I'll give you a new name": the *Satan*. That worked for many years, until people found out about the *Satan*. He came crying again: "How can I do my job?" "Don't worry, I'll give you a new name": the *yetzer hara* (the evil inclination).
blocks.outOfPlace: After line 35 the class goes on as a free discussion of the chapter's point about bina; it is placed with the line it follows.

blocks.title: The snake's new names
blocks.text: That worked for many years; Rabbi Markel thinks till the Baal Shem Tov ("I can't remember the exact dates he gave"). "Nobody wants to listen to the *yetzer hara* anymore." "I'll give you a new name: the *yesh*." Later, in the days of the Alter Rebbe or the Mitteler Rebbe (he does not remember the cutoffs): "Everybody knows about the *yesh* already." "I'll give you a new name: the *hargashas hayesh*." And you should realize, the Rebbe said: the *hargashas hayesh* is the *yesh*, the *yetzer hara*, the *Satan*, the primordial snake.

blocks.text: So the *yesh* is the primordial snake, where it says *chachma* is an *ayin* and *bina* a *yesh*. The whole *yesh* of something comes from *bina*, from its left side. And upstairs, the light is called the *ayin*: the *Or Ein Sof* is the *ayin*, and the Essence is the *yesh ha'amiti*, the true *yesh*. So the good and the bad all come out of *bina*. All the *kelipos* (husks) come out of *bina*. Everything comes out of *bina*.
blocks.outOfPlace: After line 35 the class goes on as a free discussion of the chapter's point about bina; it is placed with the line it follows.

blocks.text: The only one a little the same is *netzach*: if you're losing, you want to win. But *netzach* is only in somebody who already has it; somebody not ambitious doesn't want to be ambitious. Somebody who doesn't understand wants to understand, and the whole *yesh* of people is to show they're a *mevin* in whatever it is. And there is something even *netzach* doesn't have: *bina* is the farthest from the Essence. You understand nothing about the Essence; the whole understanding is *davka* into how the *yesh* comes from the *ayin*.
blocks.outOfPlace: After line 35 the class goes on as a free discussion of the chapter's point about bina; it is placed with the line it follows.

blocks.text: Everything else, like *taanug* and *ratzon*, is not as much into the Essence as it should be, but still a little. So too *chachma*, which is *bittul*, the feeling of *hafla'a*. Even a regular person who doesn't understand that much (according to the *bina* is the *chachma*) has a little *hafla'a* toward the *Aibershter*. He is *modeh*, he acknowledges: that is why he calls Him the *Aibershter*, the One higher.

blocks.text: So with *daas* (knowledge), which means connection: nobody is as connected as he should be, but there is a little connection. None of us love the *Aibershter* how we should, but there is a certain amount of love, and of fear. *Netzach* is overcoming your bad habits to get closer to the *Aibershter*: nobody is that great at it, but everybody has a little overcoming. And *hoda'a* (acknowledgement): everybody is *modeh* to some extent... (the side ends here).

Negligible means a little is there, *batel* (nullified) in sixty, in a thousand, in a million, but still there. *Kula kamei k'la chashiv*: before the *Aibershter* it is as if it doesn't exist; not like *batel* in sixty, a kind of error, but like 1 over infinity. That is not 0: "the 1 is still a 1", only negligible.

blocks.text: People say 1 over infinity is 0 because they don't know mathematics; there is no such real formula. 1 over 2 is a half, 1 over 3 a third, 1 over 4 a quarter: as the bottom approaches infinity the numbers get smaller, more negligible, and approach 0. But it is not actually 0, because 1 is still 1.

blocks.text: They were talking about real *Yiddishkeit* and diluted *Yiddishkeit* (a student: "this is kind of like Zeno's paradox"). A guy told Shimon: what's the big deal? Put a little water in vodka and it's still vodka, just slightly weaker. Rabbi Markel told Shimon to tell him: "What if I'll give you a glass of vodka and I'll spit in it?"

blocks.title: The ocean
blocks.text: In the ocean, if I'm standing next to you, you don't care: to the ocean it's negligible, even rotten fish. But it's still there: whatever fecal matter the fishies made is totally there, the absolute amount. It is just *k'la chashiv*, considered as nothing. That is *kula kamei k'la chashiv*: there is a *kaf* there, *k'la*, *like* nothing.

blocks.text: But *ein od milvado* (there is nothing besides Him) is different. It means 100% pure alcohol: not one molecule of water, of dust, of sodium. Nothing else here. And two things are *ein od milvado*: the *Aibershter*, the actual Essence; and *bina*. In *bina* there is not one iota of understanding into the Essence, not even a negligible one: as we learned yesterday, if you understand anything at all, it is not into the Essence. That is *davka* why *bina* will take you to the Essence. *Bina* is the complete opposite of the Essence, and the Essence of *bina*, exactly the same.

blocks.text: *Chachma*, *ratzon* and everything else are not like that. There is a little *ratzon* into the Essence, so a little Essence in the *ratzon*: a *ratzon* is that you want the Essence. And the *hafla'a* of *chachma*, as he says here, is from the Essence, not from the coming of the *yesh* from the *ayin*. "Well, how much *hafla'a* do we have, or even a big guy?" "It's *k'la chashiv*, like nothing": nothing compared to the Essence, nothing compared to what he should have. But there is still a little there.

blocks.text: So with love. Avraham Avinu said, "*Anochi k'afar va'efer*," and the *Tanya* explains it as a *mashal*: burn a big tree and nothing is left but a little dust and ashes. Compared to the *chesed* of *Atzilus*, Avraham's *chesed* is like dust and ashes to the tree: as if nothing is there, but not really nothing. So with everything else: *netzach*, you overcame a little; *hod*, you are *modeh*, not as you should; *Malchus*, he does not accept the yoke of Heaven 100%, but a little is there.

blocks.text: But in *bina*, as he said: if there is any understanding there at all, it is not into the Essence. So *bina* is the exact opposite of the Essence.

blocks.question: Does this have to do with the depth above and the depth below, *omek rom* and *omek tachas*?
blocks.text: Very much; that was the next thing. The *omek rom* is the *yesh ha'amiti*, the true *yesh*; the *omek tachas* is the *yesh hagamur*, the complete *yesh*. In the Mitteler Rebbe's *maamar* *Ata Echad*, the true *yesh* is revealed *davka* in the complete *yesh*: a person who understands. From understanding he gets a *yeshus*, a sense of self, and a joy, until he is like drunk. *Bina* is wine: *yayin yesamach levav enosh*, and *bina liba*, *bina* is the heart. Wine is the secrets of the Torah, *bina*; the secrets of the secrets, *bina sheb'bina*, is *Chassidus*.

blocks.text: The *hisbonenus* of *Chassidus* is called vodka, *mashke*. Even the songs: "Don't you worry, guys, what's going to happen to our lives, we're going to end up in Las Vegas, we'll have some vodka, too." Not Las Vegas: a Russian equivalent (Mendy said Kamchatka; the Yiddish is the *kretchme*, a Russian bar; there are a few versions). A *Chassidish* song? Because vodka means *Chassidus*. *Chassidus* is sometimes called *zeks un ninetsiker*, ninety-six proof. "That's wrong." It's *hunderteker*: the real *Chassidus* is 100% alcohol.

blocks.title: The plunger: bina is the biggest vacuum
blocks.text: How can it be 100%? When your sink is plugged, you pump and create a vacuum, and the vacuum sucks it in. The biggest vacuum is *bina*. The *Aibershter* can only be in an empty place: if you're there, if there's something there, He won't come. "What do you mean?" *Davka*: He doesn't want to be there with a *yesh*. You say, that's a different kind of *yesh*. A *yesh* of *bina* is totally empty of the *Aibershter*, a total vacuum, and that sucks Him in. A 100% lack of understanding is an absolute vacuum, so it sucks Him in totally.

blocks.text: With love, a person works on himself, as in the *Chovos HaLevavos* or something like that, to feel a vacuum of love for the *Aibershter*, or a lack of fear, to bring Him in. But that is not a 100% vacuum, nor a vacuum of the Essence: he still has some. And it says that grasping any part of the *etzem* is grasping the whole *etzem*; so with a little *etzem* there, there is no vacuum: the whole *etzem* is there. *Bina* is exactly the opposite: if you have any *bina*, there is no Essence there; if there is any actual Essence, it is not *bina*.

blocks.text: "So how can it be *davka* *bina*?" Back to chapter one: why *bina*, not *chachma* or the *middos*? *Ha b'ha talya*: two equal pans of a scale. *Davka* there the true *yesh* comes into the complete *yesh*, the whole *yeshus* of people: that they understand. When people *shvitz* (boast), it's about how much they understand, "in whatever stupidity it is".

blocks.title: The Gra: "a convert who converted"
blocks.text: And on boasting, it says *b'zos yis'halel hamis'halel*; notice what it calls him. The Gra, on the laws of *Pesach*, lists who becomes obligated in the middle of *Pesach*: a minor who grew up, a slave who was freed, and a *ger shenisgayer*, "a convert who converted". The minor was a minor, then grew up; the slave was a slave, then free. It should have said "a gentile who converted". It doesn't, and from this he deduces that a convert already has the soul of a convert.

blocks.title: Praising himself: hallel and holelus
blocks.text: So here: why *yis'halel hamis'halel*? It says a wise man, a mighty man, a rich man, and then a *mis'halel*. *Hallel* is the same root as *holelus*. (A student: "self-praise.") "No, no, no." *Mis'halel* does mean he praises himself, but *hallel* also comes from *holelus*: a wild party, a wild joy of self-abandonment. ("Like meaningless joy.") Not just meaningless: totally crazy joy. There could be a reason for the joy to start with, but you're not supposed to go into *holelus*.

blocks.title: Praising himself: hallel and holelus
blocks.text: Even on *Sukkos* or *Pesach* you're not supposed to get totally drunk and go into *holelus*. Here you're allowed to; not only allowed: he's called a *mis'halel*. He does two things. He *shvitzes*, making himself a total *yesh*; and he flips out, "drinking vodka and then throwing up and falling down in it". *B'zos yis'halel hamis'halel*: here you can have joy without bounds, flip out with self-abandonment; and you can become a total *yesh*, telling everybody, "I am the greatest." *Hallelu es Hashem kol goyim*; here he does it to himself, like Cassius Clay. That is the special thing of *bina*.

blocks.text: So *bina* is special. Chapters one to three explained that all the powers, above it and below it, are activated *davka* by *bina*, and that *bina* goes both up and down. Chapter 4 explained that it is *davka* the *prat* (the particular), again *bina*. Chapter 5: there is no *chachma* without *bina*. "But there is no *bina* without *chachma* either." Yes, but the real thing is *bina*: as chapter 1 said, you can't just have a *chachma*, only start to have one; but you can be *misbonen* (contemplate), and that is where *chachma* comes from. And now he tells us that the *bina* is *nagila v'nismecha becha mamash*.

blocks.title: Opening up the aquifer
blocks.text: So the *omek tachas*, the depth below, is the spring on the *chachma* side. (A student: "Yes, but the spring from underground.") It stimulates the *chachma*, the *bina sheb'bina*. And that is what *Moshiach* will do: cut open the river into the depth of the spring, so the whole spring comes straight out. The *mabu'in d'chochmasa*, the springs, are the depth below, *bina*. But it says the inner core of the inner core of *Abba* (*chachma*) is the inner core of *Atik* (lit. the Ancient of Days).

blocks.title: Opening up the aquifer
blocks.text: The external spring is *chachma*; the aquifer is *Atik*, and the inner core of *Abba* goes into it. But the inner core of *Ima* (lit. mother), *bina*, is the inner core of *Abba*, the aquifer inside the aquifer, and opening the spring comes *davka* from *bina*. A regular *ish tevuna*, a man of *tevuna* (drawing an idea out), draws from the aquifer, as a well does. Another kind opens the whole aquifer and brings it all out, "not in pails". *Yispatchun mabu'in d'chochmasa*: *bina* did it, the *tevuna*, not *chachma*.

blocks.title: Opening up the aquifer
blocks.text: The *mabu'in d'chochmasa* come out drop by drop, through the *chalal um'chulal*. *Yispatchun* means to bring the depth out to the outside. The Flood: the aquifer came out, it wasn't a depth anymore; and the waters above the heavens came down to the open. That is done *davka* by *bina*, as chapter 1 said: the Flood came from *bina*. Not only reaching the aquifer inside the aquifer, but opening it and bringing it out on top of the earth, as in the Flood. Then *mal'ah ha'aretz de'ah es Hashem kamayim layam m'chasim*, the whole earth covered like the ocean. Bringing the aquifers out is *bina*, actually *tevuna*.

blocks.text: (They find the place.) Up to now we learned two kinds of things. The first weeping was because he doesn't understand. The next one is from the *oneg hane'lam* in *chachma*, till he totally cannot stand anything that goes against it. And that one is of *chachma*.

In 5708 (*Tashach*) the Frierdiker Rebbe (the previous Rebbe) says: *Chassidus* calls the *koach MaH* of *chachma* the *pnimiyus chachma*, the inner core of *chachma*, but that is really its outside. The real *pnimiyus chachma* is that he cannot stand that the whole world is not studying *Chassidus*, because it stands in his way. He wants to go out to Times Square, and the big billboards will have *Chassidus* on them.

sections.title: The highest weeping: the Essence does not fit in the mind
sections.summary: There is a weeping above the first two: having understood the explanation, he sees that the thing itself can never fit in his mind. That total lack, felt in a way of a *yesh* of *bina*, weighs the same as the joy he would have if he grasped the Essence; it is the vessel for the secrets of the Torah, and it is the comprehension.

phrases.he: והנה יש בכיה למעלה מזו,
phrases.en: even higher than this

phrases.he: והוא הבא מהעדר ההשגה
phrases.en: the lack of understanding

phrases.he: מחמת עוצם הפלאת והבדלת הערך,
מפני שלא יכילו כלי מוחו כו'
phrases.en: because it won't fit in his brain

blocks.text: There is a weeping higher still, and it is in *bina*, not *chachma*. The first was weeping at not understanding the explanation. The second was the *hafla'a*: he feels how far it is from his seeing. This one is not understanding because of the thing itself, not because he didn't understand it yet.

The lack of understanding in *bina* awakens the second, the *hafla'a* of *chachma*, and that awakens the third, back in understanding: now he understands that it is totally gone from him, because the vessels of his mind cannot contain it. He understood the explanation, fine, to the point of total *hafla'a*. Now he sees he is not going to understand the actual thing: it won't fit in his brain, no matter what he does.

blocks.text: When Rabbi Akiva heard the deep secrets his eyes cried tears, because his brain couldn't take them in. It is totally *bilti musag*: the more you look into it, the farther away it is. And as far as *bina* goes it is totally separate, higher even than for *chachma*: absolutely no *bina* into it. "Zero. Absolute zero."

phrases.he: שמזה דוקא לבו דואג ובוכה.
שאינו בא רק מעוצם התענוג והתשוקה להשיג,
ואינו יכול כו'
וידוע שזהו עיקר בחינת הכלי לבחינת חכמה ברזין דאורייתא
phrases.en: that's *davka* the *kli* for the *chachma* in *razin d'oraysa*

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין אין מוסרין רזי תורה
אלא למי שלבו דואג בקרבו כו'
phrases.en: somebody whose heart is worrying inside of him

blocks.text: Why? What does *bina* want to understand? Why did he start learning *Chassidus*? He wants to understand G-d. It is exactly the opposite, as when his family went to the airport and left: the loss he feels, crying, is exactly how much pleasure he had when they were there.

This is *davka* the *kli* for the *chachma* in the secrets of the Torah, a *chachma* that comes after the *bina*: not a *chachma* of *bittul*, but actually knowing, like the Arizal, or like the Rebbe.

On *ein mosrin razei Torah*: how could you understand, if it is not possible? *Mosrin*, it is given over to him. He can't understand it, but the *Aibershter* can give it to him, because the *Aibershter* is the *Aibershter*, and He does understand it, in a way of an explanation. *Ein mosrin razei Torah ela l'mi shelibo do'eg b'kirbo*: to one whose heart worries inside him that he can't understand the *Aibershter*.

All this can happen only through *hisbonenus*. You can't say, "I want to understand the *Aibershter*? This is a lie, I'm just starting in *Chassidus*; you told me yourself it won't explain it anyway." These are three levels, one coming from the other.

phrases.he: אבל כשהיה משיג לעצמות אור אין סוף ממש,
phrases.en: but if he was *masig* to the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof mamash*

phrases.he: שם הוא ענין השמחה בעצמותו
phrases.en: there the *inyan* is of the *simcha* in the *Atzmus*

blocks.text: He is crying totally, because he has zero comprehension of the *Aibershter*. But if he would comprehend the *atzmus Or Ein Sof mamash*, the *atzmus umahus* of the *Aibershter*, there it is the joy in the Essence. "What do you mean, if he would understand?" Since there can be crying at its lack, that lack is the same as the joy: as much as he misses the people, that's how much he enjoys them.

phrases.he: ואף על פי שהוא גלוי העונג האלה״י הבא במורגש דווקא,
אבל שרשו באמת בעצמות התענוג הנעלם,
שממנו יצא היפוכו שהוא הבכיה מהעדרו

שהוא הבכיה העמוקה כשלא יכילו כלי מוחו להשיג כנזכר לעיל ודי למבין.

blocks.text: It is a joy, not a *bittul*: the joy of comprehension is a felt delight. *Bittul*, as he said, is a delight not felt; he doesn't feel he's there, and doesn't even feel that. This he feels. The weeping and the lack are the same: a thing totally non-understandable.

As in *bina* and in the *bittul* of *chachma* everything weighs *mamash* the same, so here: the total lack of understanding, because it is not understandable, the total weeping it brings, and the total happiness he would have if he understood the *Aibershter* Himself weigh *mamash* the same.

How much he would enjoy it if he actually comprehended Him: *v'hayinu hach*, it is the same thing, as in love. How much he misses the people is how much he'll enjoy them; somebody he doesn't enjoy he won't miss, and the reverse. So how much he would enjoy understanding the *Aibershter mamash* is how much he cries at not understanding. This is activated only by the *hafla'a* of *chachma*: *bina* activates *chachma*, and *chachma* activates *bina* again, a higher *bina*. Now he gives the order of the levels: not "Okay, well, I miss the *Aibershter*," but levels.

sections.title: The order of the levels, and why the not-understanding is the vessel
sections.summary: Joy from what is comprehended and weeping when it is hidden; above it the hidden delight of *chachma* and disgust with all life; above that the joy of "they will rejoice in You" and the weeping when the mind cannot hold it. The power of *bina* is the power of not understanding, like a bow drawn back: the empty glass is the vessel, and only learning makes the emptiness felt.

phrases.he: ונמצא סדר המדרגות בדבר והיפוכו כך הם,
חדוה ושמחה מגלוי אור אלה״י המושג ממש,
והיפוכו יוצא בכיה בהסתר המנגד לזה
ולמעלה מזה בבחינת ענג וחדוה הנעלם שבכח מ''ה דחכמה בעצמות אלהו״ת המהווה כו',
וכחו בהיפוכו יוצא למאוס בחייו ובחיי כל זולתו,
phrases.en: not only his own life, he can't stand the whole world

phrases.he: כמו מי לי כו'

blocks.text: So the *seder hamadreigos* (the order of the levels) in a thing and its opposite goes up and down like this. The first is in explanation, and its opposite: he doesn't understand the explanation well yet, because it is hard.

Higher is the *koach MaH* of *chachma*, and its opposite: not only his own life, he can't stand the whole world, anybody doing anything but learning *Chassidus*. Nothing matters to him; he doesn't want to know from the angels. "Why don't you calm down? We'll send you to heaven." "I don't want to go to heaven."

phrases.he: ולמעלה גם מזה
phrases.en: and even higher than this

phrases.he: הענג והחדוה העצמיים בעצמות אלהו״ת דוקא,
כמו וישמחו בך ממש בגלוי כו'
phrases.en: they will actually have *simcha* in the *Atzmus mamash* in a revealed way

phrases.he: כוחו בהיפוכו יוצא כאשר לא יכילו כלי מוחו להכיל כו',
phrases.en: the opposite of *yismechu becha mamash* is when his brain cannot take it in

phrases.he: יבכה
phrases.en: then he will cry

blocks.text: Higher still is the joy of *yismechu becha mamash b'giluy*: joy in the Essence *mamash*, revealed, in comprehension, with an explanation. "Where is the explanation?" Here: this book is explanation. And the opposite of *yismechu becha mamash* is when his brain cannot take it in: then he will cry.

phrases.he: (וכמו בכיה דאוהב הנאמן בנפשו בהפרדו,
כדוד ויהונתן דאהבת נפשו אהבו,
דכתיב וישקו ויבכו כו'
phrases.en: since they were separated, they cried

phrases.he: שבא מכח ריבוי אהבה בתענוג הגדול שביחודם ודבוקם כו' וכה"ג).
phrases.en: that's how happy they were to be together

blocks.text: Like David and Yehonasan, like the airport: *vayishku vayivku*. Separated, they cried, because of how happy they were together. Exactly the same thing.

And that is *davka* the *kli* for the comprehension; not just the *kli*: it is the comprehension. As we said, unlike many other things, in understanding the whole power of understanding comes from not understanding.

How much you realize you don't understand is how much power you get to do *hisbonenus* and understand. Why are we studying? Because we don't understand; the *hisbonenus* is from not understanding. *Bina sheb'bina*, *pnimiyus bina*, the inner core of *bina*, is the power of not understanding: the *bina* is as strong as you think you don't understand. A person who thinks he understands everything: "how much could there be already to understand by the *Aibershter*?" It is almost self-obvious. That's why you're learning.

blocks.title: Going to college to be a doctor
blocks.text: *Bina sheb'bina* means to learn. "I'm going to college." "What are you learning?" "To be a doctor." That means I don't know yet how to be a doctor: learning is learning what you don't understand.

So it goes by how much he doesn't understand in G-dliness. Learning *Chassidus*, first he cries that the explanation is so hard. Then, by how much he understands, he senses how far away it is: not just hard but impossible to understand, not an understandable thing in the first place. That is the real power of *bina*, and it awakens it: as much as he doesn't understand, that's how much he will understand.

blocks.title: The bow and the arrow
blocks.text: It goes by the negative power, like a bow and arrow: the more you pull back, the farther the arrow flies. Pull it back to total non-understanding, absolutely zero in *bina*, and it goes directly into what the zero is in: the Essence.

blocks.title: That night the king could not sleep
blocks.text: The Frierdiker Rebbe has a *maamar*, *Balayla hahu nadedah shnas hamelech*. In the Megillah you say that verse louder, because that was the essence of the whole miracle: Achashverosh couldn't sleep. "What about before? Vashti died; wasn't the main miracle when Esther became queen?" He explains in *Chassidus*: *balayla hahu* is the exile, and *hamelech*, wherever it says it in the Megillah, is the King of the world.

blocks.title: That night the king could not sleep
blocks.text: The exile is *dormita d'Zeir Anpin*, the sleep of *Zeir Anpin* (lit. the small countenance; *dormir*, to sleep). Awake, the head is above and the feet below; asleep, everything is on one level, and the feet think they're like the head, because they are. The *middos* are mixed up: the brain does not control *chesed*, *gevura*, *tiferes* or *netzach*, *hod*, *yesod*; it can be the opposite. That is dreams: they come from the liver, from *netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*. Of the three vessels, brain, heart and liver, standing up the brain is highest and the liver lowest; asleep they are level, and the liver makes up a whole bunch of dreams. "So this is very nice. And the king woke up."

blocks.title: That night the king could not sleep
blocks.text: In the future, with *Moshiach*, the King will really wake up; then, *nadedah shnas hamelech*, He woke a little and went back to sleep. "But that's all very nice. It's a very nice Kabbalistic explanation. But why does He have to sleep in the first place?" It says *hinei lo yanum v'lo yishan shomer Yisrael*, and it says *ura lama sishan*: wake up, *Aibershter*, why are You sleeping? He explains that the exile is like a dream, the dream of *Zeir Anpin*, and in a dream all kinds of crazy things happen.

blocks.title: An elephant through the eye of a needle
blocks.text: You open your door and you're in China; a tree grows down from the ceiling. But in *Shaar HaYichud* (the Gate of Unity), towards the end, where he explains dreams, the demons mix up the letters of the daytime, a letter from this word and from that: you dream at night only what you think in the day. "But an elephant through the eye of a needle you won't dream": nothing totally ridiculous. The Frierdiker Rebbe brings a quote: an elephant through the eye of a needle, where could that happen? "Only in a dream." "What are you talking about? Didn't the Mitteler Rebbe say you don't dream that?" "Yes: that's the dream from the thoughts of the heart in the daytime. That's a normal dream."

blocks.title: An elephant through the eye of a needle
blocks.text: But there are nightmares, totally crazy, nothing like the daytime. In a regular dream you don't know you're dreaming; in a terrible nightmare it's so crazy that you realize it's a dream, and you wake yourself up because you can't take it. In a nightmare an elephant can go into the eye of a needle. "And that's why the *Aibershter* went to sleep."

Because He wanted a nightmare, so we should end up in Europe, and finally in America. In a nightmare the biggest thing happens: an elephant, *pila*, the biggest animal, goes into the eye of a needle, *kufa d'machta*, the littlest thing; and the roots are *pila*, *pele*, wonder, and *machta*, *chotei*, a sinner. The *Aibershter* can go into the brain not of Rabbi Akiva, but of a normal sinner, a *rasha*, "a total American *shvantz*". Where can that happen? There was a book, "Only in America". That is the reason for the exile: the thing that can't fit in his brain. In America everything is possible. They told the Frierdiker Rebbe, "This is America."

sensitivity.reason: Calls the ordinary American sinner a "total American shvantz", a crude Yiddish word.

blocks.text: (He has to stop here.) That is the *kli*: the *kli* for actual comprehension of the Essence is the total lack of comprehension. But that lack should be felt, as a *yesh* of *bina*, not even as the *ayin* of the *hafla'a* of *chachma*; and for that you have to learn *Chassidus* first. Everybody says, "Well, I don't understand nothing in G-dliness; so I should understand G-dliness?" No: by you it is a hidden thing. You have no idea that you *mamash* understand zero, "absolutely zero". When you learn *Chassidus*, it is by way of comprehension: you don't understand anything.

That is what it means that the vessel of the mind cannot contain it. Even an elephant through the eye of a needle still has some proportion; this does not. The vessel has absolutely no room to take it in, and it is absolutely too big to go into anything. And you have to actually feel this, as a *yesh*, by way of comprehension: how much this thing is lacking in understanding. That is the *kli*.

blocks.title: A glass is its emptiness
blocks.text: You know what a *kli* is? A vacuum. The main thing of the glass is not its body but its emptiness; a full *kli* you can't put nothing into. "Everybody has a full *kli*." The real thing of proper *bina* is that it is totally devoid of G-dliness, so it is the best *kli* for G-dliness. That's why a vacuum sucks: it wants to be filled, and *bina* wants to be filled with G-dliness.

That is the main matter of *bina*: it wants to know the true nature of reality. How come people do *bina* into all kinds of other things? Look at the scientist: he wants to know the true nature of reality. The real *mevin*, the intellectual, doesn't want to know "just some stupid thing". So that's the best *kli*.

sections.title: The answer: the joy reaches the Essence, now through weeping and in the future as laughter
sections.summary: *Bina*, most opposed to the Essence, gets closest: it gives an approximation that *chachma* fills in, and the grasp is real. So the comprehension is of a *tzimtzum* while the joy is in the Essence itself; now it comes out through the weeping of exile, and in the future, eye to eye, as laughter.

phrases.he: ובכ"ז מתורץ ענין הנזכר לעיל בשמחה שבבינה וענג שבחכמה,
דגם שההשגה עצמה היא בבחינת צמצום אור האלה״י
phrases.en: not in the actual *Elokus*, and not even in the actual *or*, but in the *tzimtzum*

phrases.he: שמשיגו,
אבל השמחה שרשה מגיע בעצמות אלהו״ת דוקא
phrases.en: but what you're *sameach* in is the *Atzmus*

blocks.text: To go over it: of all the *sefiros*, *bina* has the most opposition, so it can get the closest, and the biggest weeping is in *bina*, not *chachma*. The first weeping, of *bina*, is smaller than the second, of *chachma*; but that wakes up the third, of *bina*: not that he doesn't have the explanation yet, but that now that he has it, he sees it is not into the actual Essence.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: So the longing for the *Aibershter* is strongest *davka* in *bina*: everywhere else you get a certain amount of satisfaction. The Rolling Stones song, "I can't get no satisfaction": that is *bina*, which can never get any satisfaction. In love or fear you do get some love and fear, and they are for the Essence; the *hafla'a* of *chachma* is *davka* from the Essence; so with *daas*, the upper *Keser*, *ratzon* and *taanug*. You don't grasp the Essence in them (grasping is *bina*), but they are for the Essence. In *bina*, if you understand it, it is not the Essence.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: And *bina* is like a perfect vacuum cleaner: the more you put into it, the emptier it gets. The others get a certain amount put in. There are ten kinds of *avodos* (services), one from each *sefira*, as there are ten general types of people. Each person is a mixture: down here nobody is all *chesed* or all *gevura*, but some lean more to *chesed*, some to *gevura*, some to emotions, some to brains.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: So in *avoda*: there is no *avoda* of love only, because without *hisbonenus* there is no love. Two things. First, all the *avodos* depend on *bina*, as chapter one said; that is the whole *Kuntres HaHispaalus* (the Tract on Ecstasy): no *hisbonenus*, no *avoda*. *Malchus* is accepting the yoke of Heaven; there is love and fear; *netzach* is overcoming, usually your bad habits by force of willpower; *hoda'a* is to be *modeh*. Even *hoda'a* needs some *bina*: it means you acknowledge more than you understand. That's why *hod* comes out of *bina*, as chapter thirty-three says.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: (The line has an echo.) The other thing: all the other *avodos* give a sense of satisfaction, as with eating: the more you eat, the less hungry you get, with a certain pleasure. *Bina* is the opposite: the more you feed it, the hungrier it gets. You get joy, but the *taanug* actually gets farther away.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: And the *hafla'a* of *chachma* comes *davka* from the *bina*, as these last two chapters said. Love and fear too come *davka* from *hisbonenus*, as it says in many places; it is a *halacha* in the *Rambam*, and that is how he starts his whole *Yad HaChazaka*. Even accepting the yoke of Heaven, which is without intellect, needs some *bina* to get started.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: Like the song from yesterday, one the Rebbe *mamash* sang himself: *tzam'a lecha nafshi kama lecha vesari*, the thirst is spiritual and physical. How? *B'eretz tziya v'ayef bli mayim*: no water at all, which is *davka* *bina*; everywhere else it is not a pure vacuum. *Kein bakodesh chazisicha*: *kein* here means not yes but thus: through having no water at all, I see You in the holiness, *lir'os uzcha uchevodecha*. *Lir'os* (to see) is *chachma*; but a *chizayon*, like a stargazer's, is not actually seeing, not a clear sight: an approximation, a vision.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.question: You say *bina* is the opposite of the Essence, and that is why it can grasp it; but if you grasp it, it is not the Essence. So how does it grasp the Essence?
blocks.text: What *bina* actually is, is an approximation, or a simulation, like a *chizayon*. A *chizayon* is like the way you get a picture on a computer screen.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: The Rebbe's picture on the computer screen
blocks.text: His computer's background picture is the Rebbe, or any picture. Magnify it and it is pixels, a bunch of dots; bigger and bigger, and it is not really a picture of the Rebbe at all, just a bunch of details. That's *bina*: it supplies details. There is a level of clarity (he doesn't remember the computer word): 320 by 400, 600 by 800, 1200 by 1500. And some pages, downloading, don't fill in from the top down: they fill all over, a bunch of squares, and you can't see what it is yet. ("You're not such a big computer freak like me and Shimon.")
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: The Rebbe's picture on the computer screen
blocks.text: As it fills in, detail after detail, you still can't tell who it is, but you see a human face; it's all squares. More and more, and finally you *mamash* see the Rebbe's face, as if he is standing in front of you. But it is still just an approximation, the same as before: it went from 20 by 40 to 200 by 300; his own computer is older, 640 by 800 or so, and newer ones are 1200 by 1500, really sharp. But he can see the Rebbe: "It doesn't look to me like it's a bunch of pixels at all. It looks to me just like when I stood in front of the Rebbe."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: Your eyes are made of pixels
blocks.text: Think about it: right now you're looking around and seeing the room. "It's not true. It's pixels. Your eyes are made of pixels." The retina, at the back of the eye, is made of pixels of different colors that work exactly like a TV, except they are receptors. That's why after you look at the sun or a bright light you still see an afterimage: they get slightly burnt out until they regenerate.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: A movie is still pictures
blocks.text: So whatever you see, you are really seeing an approximation, as in a movie: nobody is moving at all; it's a bunch of still pictures, the details. ("It's an optical illusion.") "Well, it's not just an optical illusion; it's a little bit more than that," like the Rebbe's face on the screen.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: Close enough for folk music
blocks.text: The *chachma* fills in the spaces of the *bina*. A circle on a computer screen is not really a circle but a multi-gon, a hexagon, an octagon (eight edges), a decagon ("there are thousands of little edges"). A real circle has infinite edges, and on 640 by 800 you can't get infinite edges. But as they say, close enough for folk music: your *chachma* fills in the extra edges and you see a circle. That is what it says: the *bina* and the *chachma* work together.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: Notice how he started off; you often wonder why he opens a chapter one way and then jumps: "But first we have to do something else." In chapter five, before the rest of chapter five and chapter six, he says you have to know all the *pratim* (particulars) of *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, *v'yevo'aru kulam b'kuntres meyuchad*: he'll explain all the points. But then: you can't explain all the points. *Min hatzorech mikol prat*, what you need from every particular, *umimeila yuvan lamevin v'yeida kama pratim acherim*. I'll give you the approximation, enough points, and automatically you'll fill in the rest: you'll see a circle. That is *bina*: giving you the particulars.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: Later in the book, explaining *chachma* and *bina*, he says *chachma* comes *mimeila*, automatically: you make no effort to make it a circle, or to see the movie as moving. So too he explains later, on joining to *chachma*: *bina* dissects the idea into concepts, smaller concepts, words, all the way to letters, and transfers the letters over one at a time: the mother lends the clothing to the daughter, speech.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: Bah, boo: no word is ever said
blocks.text: Right now he is really talking one letter at a time: make a time study and "at no point did I say an actual word"; a word takes several points of time. In the book, too, there is not a single word, only letters and spaces. But your *chachma* puts it together automatically. You don't have to think, "Wait a minute, he said ah, then ooh, then bah, then boo, so that means something. If bah and boo, what does that mean? Bah-boo? Oh, okay." It happens *mimeila*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: So *kein bakodesh chazisicha*: I have the *chizayon* of You, and from it the *chachma* of *uzcha uchevodecha*, your strength and glory, already not really You: the *chachma* is into the Name, the light. "The *bina* never at any point gets the actual self." "Yes, so what? It gives you better and better approximations." "Okay, but that's still not the actual self."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.title: The voice on the telephone
blocks.text: The picture of the Rebbe is not the actual Rebbe. Right now his voice is being turned into approximations in electric pulses, and what you get over there is not exactly his voice. ("Well, it's not even your voice at all, really.") Yes, an approximation. ("Of course.") "Okay, but it makes no difference. You're talking to me, and I'm talking to you." The grasp you get is actual, approximation or not. So it is *davka* *bina* that catches the *etzem*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: That is also why, as it says in various places, *bina* is *teshuva ila'a* (the higher return). You'd think *teshuva ila'a* is a guy crying, an emotion. Why *bina*? It says *tashuv hanefesh el Havaya*, or *el Elokim* (he can't remember which): *teshuva* is to return all the way to G-d, not part of the way. Only *bina* can do that; all the others are not 100%.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: And *teshuva* has two matters: to return all the way to the *Aibershter*, and, the main thing, to realize how far away you are from Him. That is *davka* by *bina*. Only in *bina* does he realize that he has absolutely nothing to do with the *Aibershter*: all the understandings and emotions are totally nothing.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 069 opens with this discussion of bina, before it reads line 52; it leads up to the answer given in this line.

blocks.text: (They find the place, a little past the middle of page 226.) The order of the levels: the weeping of *bina*, because he doesn't understand the explanation yet; the weeping of *chachma*, at the *hafla'a*, how far it is; and finally the weeping of *bina*, because it is totally not understandable. The comprehension is not in G-dliness itself, nor in the light, but in the *tzimtzum* of the light.

גם השגתם באה על ידי צמצום כידוע
וזהו וישמחו בך דוקא,
phrases.en: actually in the *Atzmus*

phrases.he: והיינו חדווא בסטרא דא ובכיה היפוכה יוצא מכחה בג' מיני מדריגות הנזכר לעיל
וב' קווין שקולין הם
phrases.en: these are the exact two sides of the same thing

phrases.he: בשווה ממש
phrases.en: exactly equal

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: That is what *v'yismechu becha davka* means: actually in the Essence. These are exactly the two sides of the same thing, exactly equal.

phrases.he: וזהו בשמחה ובטוב לבב מרוב כל,
phrases.en: that you will worship the *Aibershter* *b'simcha uvtuv levav*, from having so much of everything

phrases.he: בהשגת המהוה
phrases.en: actual *hasaga*, not of the *mis'haveh* but of the *mehaveh*

blocks.text: That is *b'simcha uv'tuv levav merov kol*: you will serve the *Aibershter* with joy and gladness of heart from the abundance of everything, an actual comprehension not of what is brought into being but of the One who brings it into being. It starts off only into what is brought into being; finally you'll have the whole thing, the comprehension of the One who brings into being, actually.

phrases.he: וכמו לעתיד דכתיב עין בעין נראה כו'
phrases.en: you'll *mamash* see the *Aibershter* eye to eye

phrases.he: ואמר ביום ההוא הנה אלהינ״ו זה,
phrases.en: right in front of us, this is this

phrases.he: לנוכח,
phrases.en: right in front of us

phrases.he: אז נגילה ונשמחה בו דווקא כידוע ודי למבין
אבל עכשיו כל זה בוקע ויוצא על ידי המנגד,
phrases.en: right now it's *davka* to the opposite

phrases.he: היפוכו דוקא, שהוא הבכיה מסטרא דא
עד רום המעלות וכמו שכתוב בבכי יבואו דוקא,
וכן הלוך ילך ובכה כו'

blocks.text: In the future, *ayin b'ayin yir'u*: you'll *mamash* see the *Aibershter* eye to eye. *V'amar bayom hahu hinei Elokeinu zeh*: right in front of us, *this* is this. Not *koh*, "like this": this is the *Aibershter*. We'll be able to say the exact thing, right in front of us. And then, when *Moshiach* comes, *nagila v'nismecha*. But now, right now, it is precisely the opposite: *bivchi yavo'u davka*, *haloch yelech uvacho*.

This is also exile and redemption. ("Just one minute.") The comprehension is of a *tzimtzum* of G-dly light, but what you rejoice in is the Essence. "Yes, but it's more than that": finally the comprehension will be in the Essence, because it is a *mashal* on a *mashal*, *ulehavin davar mitoch davar*. From the externality of the One who brings into being he will comprehend Him, not what is brought into being, climbing the levels in *bina*.

That's first of all. The joy we are getting from *bina* is not from understanding psychological concepts, how the human mind works; "we're not interested in that at all, actually." Even now, in these contracted comprehensions, the joy is in G-d Himself, the *bo*. It makes no difference.

The joy is that we are slowly getting the *chizayon* of G-dliness filled in: one little detail, another, and slowly we see a picture. Even in a detail, the joy is from the G-dliness in it, the *nimshal* (what the analogy stands for), not the *mashal*. "Oh, the light of the sun: there's this fantastic explosion." "So who cares?"

And in the exile and the redemption: what did the *Aibershter* see to pick *davka* "idiots like us", when *bina* is from the highest things? Guys who, by the levels of how they used to be, don't have no *middos* and not much of a *sechel* (intellect) either. Why? First, with no *middos* to interfere, we can get no sense of accomplishment or enjoyment from anywhere but the *bina*. And in *bina*, the more he doesn't understand, the more he is connected to G-dliness.

We don't understand better than any previous generation. ("Yeah, we're pretty good at not understanding.") "We're total idiots," and not just us: the whole generation. Why not pick the older generations, who could have understood better? *Davka* because of that: the sense of not understanding is strongest by us, the farthest away. So *teshuva ila'a*, the *yichudim* (unifications), everything is *davka* from *bina*. *Bina* is the central... (the side ends here).

As he said, this chapter is "really a fantastic chapter" for pulling together the whole beginning of the book: of the *avodos*, it is *davka* *bina*, for two reasons. One: any other *avoda* you choose also depends on *bina*. The *avoda* of love and fear is really also *hisbonenus*, because *bina* awakens all the other faculties: you can't have love and fear without it, and even an *avoda* of *hafla'a* is only through *bina*. So whichever way you look at it, the main *avoda*, even of the other nine, is *bina*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 070 opens with this, before it rereads lines 58-60.

blocks.text: Then there is the *avoda* of *bina* itself. The others are, in a way, *avodas halev* (the service of the heart), and even that is really *bina*; but *avodas hamochin* is pure *bina*, unconnected with the emotions. Even the highest *avoda*, *daas Havaya* (knowing G-d), is *davka* *bina*, not an *avoda* of *daas*: *daas* is the result, as when he told them he couldn't sleep because his mind was all fired up and he couldn't remove the focus. The actual *avoda* is *bina*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 070 opens with this, before it rereads lines 58-60.

blocks.text: Grasping the knowledge of the Essence is exactly the opposite of what people say. "After all, the Essence is totally non-understandable": true, not just hard but beyond understanding. But the conclusion they draw is the main point of the breaking of the vessels, which is in *bina*, SaG of SaG: *bina* is the source of the *kelipos*, of the breaking and of the repair, the eighth king of *Tohu*. They concluded: since *bina* is not into the Essence at all, stay away from *bina* and go to *daas*. Instead of the Tree of Life he ate from the Tree of Knowledge. "It's basically shoe on head": that *bina*, more than any *sefira*, is not into the Essence is what makes it have the most to do with the Essence. It sucks the Essence into it.
