From the weeping of the exile will come the laughter of the coming of *Moshiach*.

sections.title: Tikkun chatzos: the simple tear over the sins of youth prepares the way
sections.summary: The plain tears of the midnight lament over the sins of youth repair the source of the flaw, the casting off of the yoke, and become bread for prayer; they are the first step and the preparation for the three levels of weeping, the work the *shluchim* do in the world today.

phrases.he: ובכל זה יובן טעם האמיתי לענין תיקון חצות בבכיה דוקא
שהוא תועלת לנפש להיות בתפילה גילוי תענוג העצמי, כמו וישמחו בך וכהאי גוונא
והגם שהבכיה בתיקון חצות הוא דמעות פשוטים על חטאות נעורים וכהאי גוונא,
phrases.en: it's just a plain crying on his *chatos ne'urim*, on the sins of his youth

phrases.he: אבל על זה אמר היתה לי דמעתי לחם יומם ולילה
phrases.en: the *dim'a* of the *tikkun chatzos* will be the *lechem* of the *yomam valayla*

blocks.text: By the way, these two chapters, on the weeping and the joy more than on *bina*, the tears and the *chatos ne'urim* (the sins of youth), are expanded into basically a whole book in *Derech Chaim*.

blocks.title: The plane from Los Angeles to New York
blocks.text: The simple tears over the sins of youth are *mamash* the same thing as going towards the Essence. You fly from Los Angeles to New York, 3,000 miles, and the guy on the plane says, "We've gone 1,000 miles from Los Angeles." "And how much closer to New York are we?" "Idiot, I told you, we're 1,000 miles farther from Los Angeles. So we have to be 1,000 miles closer to New York." On a line, how far you left from where you're leaving is how close you got to where you're going.

So as far as you went from the sins of youth, that's how close you're getting to the *Aibershter*, *mamash* the same thing. So of this weeping, plain crying over his sins of youth, it says *haysa li dim'asi lechem yomam valayla*,

phrases.he: בקריאת שמע ותפילה דשחרית וערבית כו'
phrases.en: of the *Krias Shema* of *Arvis* and *Shachris*: *yomam* is *Shachris* and *laila* is *Arvis*

phrases.he: מפני שהדמעות על הריחוק שלו מעוונות וחטאים שלו מתקנים בחינת מקור הפגם,
שהוא דוקא פריקות עול מלכות שמים,
ובחינת גלות השכינה הוא בא בדרך פרט בכל ניצוץ אלה״י
phrases.en: this thing of the general *golus haShechina* comes in a particular way in each divine *nitzotz*

blocks.text: The tear of *tikkun chatzos* (the midnight lament) will be the bread of *yomam valayla*: of the *Shema* of *Maariv* and *Shacharis*. *Yomam* is *Shacharis*, and *layla* is *Maariv*. Why?

*Derech Chaim* covers all this at very great length, and *Shaarei Orah* tells how the tear repairs the *makor hapgam*, the source of the flaw. The crying over the sins is really over their reason, the *perikas ol* (casting off the yoke) of Heaven. The general exile of the *Shechina* comes into each G-dly spark: there is a spark of the *Shechina* in exile there.

phrases.he: והדמעה הזאת תתקן ותעביר הפגם לגמרי
ותעורר למעלה בחינת הבכיה שמנגד
ובא מכח היפוכו,
phrases.en: and this comes from the opposite

phrases.he: שהוא החדוה העצמית הנזכר לעיל
להאיר בנפשו האלהי״ת בקריאת שמע ותפילה כו'
להיות ממש כמו לחם לנפשו כו'
phrases.en: this crying of leaving the sins becomes *mamash* like actual food for his soul

blocks.text: This comes from the opposite. Notice that now he is talking about *teshuva tata'a* (the lower return), of *Malchus*; before it was *teshuva ila'a*. Even *teshuva tata'a*, simply crying about the sins, can bring him to G-dliness, but it is nothing like *teshuva ila'a*. The crying over leaving the sins becomes *mamash* food for his soul.

phrases.he: ולהיפוך בפריקות עול, היפך הדמעה,
phrases.en: and exactly the opposite is the *prikas ol*, which is the opposite of crying

phrases.he: כמו והתברך בלבבו
phrases.en: he thinks he's blessed

phrases.he: בשרירות לבי אלך כו'
phrases.en: I will go in the mastery of my heart; I'll do whatever I feel like

phrases.he: כעבד שמורד,
phrases.en: when an *eved* is *mored*

phrases.he: שהמרידה ופריקות עול עיקר ומקור לכל שיעשה נגד רצון האדון כו':

blocks.text: Exactly the opposite of crying is the *perikas ol*. Of a guy who casts off the yoke it says *hisbarech bilvavo*: he thinks he's blessed. "Eh, nothing could happen to me. I'll do whatever I feel like." He walks around like a big shot, *k'eved shemored*: a servant who rebels and seems to be succeeding, strutting around.

But *bina* is *teshuva ila'a*, which totally includes this. Especially in our days a person doesn't even understand that he casts off the yoke, or how he could, as if he understood that the master is standing right there. Why not? Because he has no *hisbonenus*. He doesn't know that he doesn't know, so he blesses himself: "I'm safe. I got away, and I can do whatever I want now."

phrases.he: והנה על זה אמר אוילים מדרך פשעם.
phrases.en: the *evilim* will leave the *derech pisham*

phrases.he: פשעים אלו המרדים בפריקת עול,
phrases.en: a *pesha* means that it's not just something that's done, but it's done in a way of a *mered*; a *mered* is rebellion, with a *prikas ol*, that he's taken off the yoke

phrases.he: גם שיתענו מעונותיהם בחטאות נעורים,

"A *poshei'a*") is not just something done, but done as a *mered*, a rebellion, casting off the yoke. Even though they fast and think they're leaving the sins of youth (*Derech Chaim* explains this at great length), what's it going to help them? Because they don't want to learn *Chassidus*. "So what's it going to help them to beat their chest?"

The crying really comes from understanding what he did; and this is the opposite of *oneg*, the crying is the opposite of *oneg*, which will enliven his soul. *Yagi'u ad sha'arei maves*: they will come till the gates of death.

blocks.text: The crying of *tikkun chatzos* is the crying over the exile. The real crying over the exile is not, as the *Rambam* rules, wanting *Moshiach* for all the goodies; it is being far from the *Aibershter*: he cast off the yoke, so now he has no room to study properly. This prepares the three levels that come later: this crying of *teshuva* is just a beginning, the *teshuva tata'a*.

But none of this part applies nowadays, because we're doing *lechatchila ariber*. Yet even with the Rebbe, going *lechatchila ariber*, you have to know what you're jumping over. *Teshuva tata'a*, leaving the sins, does apply; it is just done without weeping.

blocks.question: According to the Rebbe, isn't there still a weeping over the exile, only not over the sins?
blocks.text: No: the Rebbe said no more weeping over the exile. "You don't have to do the weeping anymore, now we're doing the joy already": *Moshiach* is coming. Nor over the sins of youth: just leave them. And that is one reason not to go against the *shluchim* (the Rebbe's emissaries): they're preparing everybody for us.

This is the first level: these people have to put on *tefillin* and keep *Shabbos*. Leaving the sins of youth prepares the three weepings: of *bina*, at the hard basic explanations; of *chachma*, at how far the *Aibershter* is; of *bina* again, at the totally incomprehensible. The preparation is the weeping of *tikkun chatzos*, which gets him to leave the sins of youth.

Right now it is very important to remember the *shluchim*, all over the place, getting people to take the first step of *teshuva*. For the external world they are basically saving it: bringing about the *teshuva tata'a*, getting people to put on *tefillin*, keep *Shabbos*, eat kosher, learn *mishnayos*, do *ChiTaS*, "and all this kind of business."

blocks.title: The shliach from Singapore
blocks.text: At the *shluchim* convention in New York this weekend, someone met an old yeshiva friend, now the *shliach* of Singapore, who had brought a *gvir* (a wealthy man) with him from Singapore who studies in a cyber yeshiva. These are the guys who supply you guys: a *shliach* went out there first and started the place, and now there's kosher food and a synagogue for you. So it's very important.

That's the preparation, not like the hermetic Kabbalists who just study *Kabbala*: "No, you have to put on *tefillin*," and eat kosher. ("But even that you can go *lechatchila ariber*.") Yes, once you start eating kosher; but a guy not doing *teshuva* enough to eat kosher is not really studying *Chassidus*. That's what he says next.

sections.title: The sign of the true thing: the lower return, our days, and the tevuna of the Essence
sections.summary: Without the preparation a man fools himself: weeping alone, joy alone, or neither deep, and it does not last. A *Chassidus* that does not make a man more observant is not *Chassidus*; in our days the Rebbe says to go over the top, without weeping. And what is learned here is the *tevuna* of the Essence itself, given down to the lowest.

blocks.text: Somebody who really wants to be close to the *Aibershter*... And he shouldn't fool himself, to *mamash* lose his soul for nothing.

Now it's no longer *tikkun chatzos*, but there is doing *teshuva*. The sign: without *teshuva tata'a* there's no real *teshuva ila'a*. You can't study *Chassidus* and not become *frummer* (more observant); if it doesn't make you *frummer*, it's not *Chassidus*. ("A totally different *Chassidus*.") It might be *Chassidus*, but you didn't learn it properly. The Frierdiker Rebbe calls it *Chassidus* from the *ba'al davar*, the adversary, "because it looks more sophisticated."

*Tikkun chatzos* is the weeping over the sins of youth, the most external level of *teshuva*. Now the Rebbe said *teshuva* is no longer done by weeping. That was until the Frierdiker Rebbe, whose motto was *l'alter l'teshuva, l'alter l'geula*, immediately to *teshuva*, immediately to the redemption; in our days, the Rebbe says, it is *l'alter l'geula*.

blocks.question: Doesn't that disagree with what he says here, that there is no joy without weeping?
blocks.text: No: the weeping was in the exile. "We already did the crying, and now we're ready for happiness." It is still there: in the exile the weeping was open and the joy hidden; now the joy is open and the weeping hidden. But *tikkun chatzos*, fixing the sins of youth, is the basic level of *teshuva*: without it a person is not really studying *Chassidus*.

blocks.title: The letter from Toronto
blocks.text: He got a letter from a young *Lubavitcher bochur* (young man). His father is getting mixed up with Bnei Baruch, a close sister group of the Berg people, also Ashlagians. He looked through their stuff: "they're total heretics." And the boy wonders what's happening, because his father seems more and more lax with the *mitzvos*.

sensitivity.reason: Calls a named Kabbala movement "total heretics".
sensitivity.publishable: He got a letter from a young man whose father is getting involved with a popular Kabbala movement, and the son is wondering what's happening, because it looks like his father is becoming more and more lax with the *mitzvos*.

blocks.text: That's the sign, he's telling you: if he's becoming lax with the *mitzvos*, it's not real *Kabbala* or *Chassidus*. You can't say, "But I'm doing *Kabbala*, I'm doing *teshuva ila'a*." *Teshuva ila'a* automatically includes the *teshuva tata'a*, and your doing of the *mitzvos* should automatically improve.

ולקבלת כל רזין כו' כמו שכתוב בקונטרס באריכות ודי למבין):

blocks.text: He begins the chapter's last paragraph, on the Maggid. They stop at a word their copy has unclearly ("It's kind of unclear."), and the tape is turned over.

He thinks it's a mistake, a typo; it might be *tivi'im*. ("What does *tivi'im* mean? The natural scientists or something like that?" "I don't know. We got stuck on this word also.") From what follows, it must be the *bechiya hativ'is*, the natural weeping: the simple crying he spoke of before. (Is there a footnote there, on the sins of youth? There is not.)

The basic point of the end part is that *teshuva tata'a* is a necessary *kli*, a preparation, for learning the deeper *Chassidus*. In the Mitteler Rebbe's way, you couldn't understand *Chassidus* properly without a big preparation, with crying and stuff like that. The Rebbe says now it is different: the Rebbe Maharash said *lechatchila ariber*, and the Rebbe said two, the Rebbe Maharash's and his own, which is to start living like *Moshiach*. (He will look up after the footnote on *v'chmo shekasav haRav haMaggid*, in the *Maamarim Kuntreisim*.)

To recap the chapter: at the end he seems to back off from the beginning. *Bina* was the main thing; then it switched to the *avoda* of *Malchus*, from *teshuva ila'a* to *teshuva tata'a*. But notice: "This is the preparation for what I said before. If you're not doing the *mitzvos*, then you're not doing nothing. It all goes together with being *frum*." If you're not *frum*, you have to start along with this, or the whole thing won't work. And what Shimon said, that the Rebbe says now it's *lechatchila ariber*, is because now everybody is a *tinok shenishba* (a child taken captive), with no real sins of youth. That's why it can work.

blocks.title: "Hey, king-o baby, let's dance"
blocks.text: You can't rebel against the kingdom and at the same time do a *teshuva ila'a*: "Hey, king-o baby, let's dance together." "What are you talking about? You're a rebel against the kingdom, I'm going to hang you. A rebel is a rebel: you cast off the yoke." But now they are not rebels.

The Rebbe gave various reasons. Also, the weeping was already done, the whole exile: since what happened, especially in the Second World War, the Jews had such a weeping that it's time for the joy. The Rebbe is not disagreeing with this; he just adjusted it for our days.

We know from our own experience that you can do *lechatchila ariber* and go straight to *daas Havaya*, which is what the Rebbe means by starting to live like *Moshiach*: in the time of *Moshiach*, *daas Havaya* is the only thing everybody will do. He reads the footnote from the Maggid: it is the *malchus shamayim hativ'is* (the natural kingship of Heaven), rooted in him from his youth. That too is not so anymore. He means that for a person who didn't *mamash* grow up *frum*, it's very hard to become a guy who learns these things and is actually affected by them.

But the Rebbe said it's not like that by us anymore. The chapter began on *bina* and *teshuva ila'a*, and ended: no *teshuva ila'a* without *teshuva tata'a* first. That was until the Rebbe Maharash, whose *lechatchila ariber* means forget the *teshuva tata'a* and go straight to *teshuva ila'a*. The Rebbe went farther: forget even the *teshuva ila'a*; we're going to *pnimiyus bina*, the inner core of *bina*, into the actual Essence. And that's chapter 6.

"It's a very fantastic chapter." Its main point: *bina*, basically the study of this book, of explanations, *davka* because it does not grab onto the Essence of G-dliness at all (all *bina* can do is understand explanations, and if you understand it, it is not the Essence), awakens *bina liba*: with the eye of the intellect in the heart everything is seen. And the heart sees *davka* with *bina*.

So *bina* is the perfect vacuum cleaner, and more: the more you put in, the bigger the vacuum gets. The more he understands, the more he sees there's nothing there, just an explanation. *Davka* that is the *kushya*, the difficulty, of *bina*: he really wants to understand the thing itself, not just the explanation.

You can see this in your own *bina*: you want to understand the actual thing, not just the explanation. So the first difficulty is that he doesn't understand the explanation yet. When he does, that immediately brings the flash of *chachma*, in which he sees the *hafla'a*, what he didn't understand, and how far it is from understanding. This brings the second *kli* of *bina*, the third *kli*: not that he doesn't understand the explanation (he understands it perfectly), but that he cannot understand the Essence. Then what? He can't understand the Essence, but the Essence can make itself understood: the *Aibershter* is all-powerful.

That's why it says *mosrin*: he doesn't get it himself; it's given to him. That is the whole matter of Torah: *Moshe kibel Torah miSinai umesarah liYehoshua*. Through his own effort Moshe reached the level to receive it, but the Torah itself is totally beyond Moshe; called the Torah of Moshe, it comes from the *Aibershter* and includes everything, written and oral. On the oral Torah too it says *vayomer Hashem el Moshe*: it was also given to Moshe. And it will be opened up by *Moshiach*; this is that opening up, and it is into the Essence.

"If it's so simple, the explanation is right here in front of us: it was already given, here it is, and anybody can grab it." No, they can't. People who don't even have the preparation, who don't put on *tefillin* every day and eat pig, so "their whole brain is made out of pig meat."

sensitivity.reason: Says of Jews who do not keep the mitzvos that their brain is "made out of pig meat".

blocks.text: *Davka* because of this, *bina* connects all the way up: all the *binos* connect, more than other things. *Chachma* coming down from the *Ein Sof* through *Atzilus* and *Beriya* to this world is not *mamash* the same *chachma* anymore, though all of it is the *Aibershter*'s; certainly *chesed*: Avraham's love was not like the love upstairs. But what we learn here is the explanation of the *Aibershter* Himself. "But it came down many levels." "*Davka* that shows it is the *tevuna* of the *Ein Sof* Himself."

Not a lower *tevuna* of *Asiya*: just the opposite, that it came down so far that even we can understand it shows it is the *tevuna* of the *Ein Sof*, who came up with this explanation. As we learned, *davka* the *ish tevuna* can bring the water to the sheep. Other things come through *hishtalshelus*; this comes direct. "But there's a *hislabshus*, an enclothing, into *meshalim*, and the *meshalim* into *meshalim*, and the *meshalim* into *meshalim*." Yes, but the *tevuna* itself has no enclothing. It's *mamash* the *tevuna* of the *Aibershter*.

That is the whole matter of *tevuna*: to enclothe it in *meshalim* until a little baby can understand. So it says of the Ark in the Holy of Holies in the first Temple: *Malchus* of *Atzilus* was enclothed only in *Malchus* of *Beriya*, and the *Shechina* was actually there, with no further enclothing into *Yetzira* and *Asiya*: basically the last chapter of the *Tanya*.

This book is higher than the Holy Ark: the actual *tevuna* of the *Ein Sof*. "But it goes through the levels of enclothing." That is the whole matter of *tevuna*. *Lisvunaso ein cheker*: His *tevuna*, beyond searching, can explain what is beyond searching, like a *tzimtzum*, and He wanted to explain it to us. So the enclothing in *meshalim* is *mamash* the *tevuna* itself. "This is the *tevuna* of the *Aibershter* literally": the explanation itself is the Essence.

"How? If you can understand it, it's not the Essence." Here you've got to go that extra step: *pesi ya'amin l'chol davar*. The *Aibershter* wanted to explain to us what a *tzimtzum* was and everything, and did; that is this book. It is His own explanation, *pnimiyus haTorah*, not even from *Malchus* of *Atzilus* but from the *Ein Sof* Himself: "It's *mamash* the *Ein Sof* is standing here and explaining it to us."

As it says, *Kudsha Brich Hu v'Oraysa v'Yisrael kula chad*. This is *mamash* the inner Torah, the *shaashua hamelech b'atzmuso*, the King's delight in Himself. David called it *sha'ashu'im* and was punished, but he was speaking of the delights on the outside. This is not the explanation of the world: it is G-d's explanation of Himself.

That's why we're absolutely invincible. We're not going with the light of *Atzilus*, or the lights of *Tohu* and vessels of *Tikkun*, not with lights at all: with the *Maor* (the source of light) itself, literally. *Chassidus*. Where do you get such a crazy thing? All over *Chassidus* it says *Chassidus* is the *Maor*: the *Chassidus* itself is the *Aibershter*. And *Inyana shel Toras HaChassidus* says *Moshiach*, *Chassidus*, the *Aibershter* and the Rebbe are all one thing.

Chapter 6, before chapter seven, has two main matters. One is joy and weeping in general, which applies in all the *sefiros* and any *avoda*: basically the matter of the *Keser*. The *Keser* of a *sefira* means that as bad as you feel for not having it, that's how good you feel having it: its *taanug*.

blocks.text: And by the *taanug* will be the *ratzon*: if you feel real bad, you want it real bad. This applies later too, when we get to the *Kesarim* (the crowns): *ratzon* and *taanug* are the same thing, but the *ratzon* comes from the opposite of the *taanug*, *davka* the weeping part. The more you lack the *taanug*, the stronger the *ratzon*; when you get what you want, you're satiated. So, as he was saying, *davka* when he feels the lack he will study harder, for instance.

blocks.text: So in any *midda*, like the guys who go for the Olympics. Why do they try so hard? Because they feel a lack that others don't ("I could care less"), because if they won they would feel the great enjoyment. As far as he's concerned, if he would win the spitting contest, "what do I care?" So weeping and joy are like that in all the *sefiros*, not just *bina*.

blocks.text: But in *Chassidus*, in weeping and joy, *bina* is the strongest: there is absolutely no satiation, no *taanug*. The more you understand, the more you see it is beyond understanding totally, so the lack grows the more you get it; the more you understand, the more you want. In *bina* it is infinite, because the lack is 100%: if you understand it, it's not the Essence. In the others, like the *hafla'a*, the insight is into the Essence itself.

blocks.text: So the *hafla'a* is *davka* the Essence, and so is the accepting of the yoke of Heaven, from the end of the chapter: they get a certain amount. By *bina* it's "totally, totally gone".

blocks.text: But *bina* always has two sides, as in chapter two: *bina* and *tevuna*. In *bina* itself (the whole chapter there talks about it a lot) they are from down to up, the receiver, the student, and from up to down, the teacher. *Bina* is from down to up, because *bina* means to understand the actual thing: you're going up. That is *hisbonenus*: learning, the student going up.

blocks.text: That whole chapter also explains a *hisbonenus* of the teacher, how to teach the thing; but that is the *hisbonenus* of *tevuna*, *tevuna sheb'tevuna*, not *bina sheb'bina*, because you're not trying to understand it. For *tevuna* you already have to understand it, and now he contemplates it to get a good *kelita*, a good hold of it. In general *bina* goes up from the student to the teacher, and *tevuna* is, by its definition, that the *ish tevuna* can teach it to others: *mayim amukim yidlenah ish tevuna*.

blocks.text: So as with *bina*: of all the ways of going up, *bina sheb'bina*, *hisbonenus*, is the strongest, because it is *mamash* directed at the Essence itself; in the others the Essence is not totally lacking, so the desire for it is not total. But he didn't talk about the other side, the *tevuna*. In the flow from the *Aibershter* down, it is *davka* *tevuna* that comes down with no enclothing whatsoever: *mayim amukim yidlenah ish tevuna*.

blocks.title: Shlomo's three thousand meshalim
blocks.text: To be an *ish tevuna*, able to explain it to somebody else, he has to understand it even better, as it explains in various places: the *tevuna* has to go into the depth of *chachma*, the inner core of *Abba*, of *Atik*. He explains later what a big *chacham* (wise man) is: Shlomo. What shows it? That he could make three thousand *meshalim*. "Wait a minute": three thousand *meshalim* is not a matter of *chachma* at all. It's *tevuna*.

blocks.title: Shlomo's three thousand meshalim
blocks.text: A *mashal* enclothes the thing, not just bringing it down but into a *davar zar*, something foreign, outside itself: a *mashal* means *tevuna*. Yet *davka* the *tevuna* proved how smart he was. So too, Moshe Rabbeinu found wise men, but men of understanding he couldn't find: *tevuna* is harder to find than *bina*. It's higher.

blocks.text: Three thousand *meshalim* means he could enclothe the *chachma* level after level, three thousand levels down. So Shlomo HaMelech is saying that the *Aibershter* Himself enclothed everything farther and farther down: the whole *seder hishtalshelus*. *Pasach Eliyahu*: why did He create the world? To show people: it's a *mashal*, explaining the *Aibershter* to people. A teaching process: as we said, the whole *tzimtzum* is like a teacher. Why did He make the *tzimtzum*?

blocks.text: Look at the others. When *chachma* comes down in three thousand *meshalim*, what reaches the end of the last *mashal* is not the *chachma* of the first, though in a way it takes a bigger *chachma* to enclothe it: it is just a very big *tzimtzum* of *chachma*. So it is in all the *sefiros*.

blocks.text: To enclothe it takes a very big power, so the power of the *tzimtzum* is at least as great as the power of the *Ein Sof*. Really it is greater, because the power of the *tzimtzum* allows the *Ein Sof* in the first place, when you're not limited. So it is *mamash* the same power, maybe greater: a power of the Essence. But the power of the *Ein Sof* is also a power of the Essence.

blocks.title: A voice that breaks a few trees
blocks.text: Even so, in all the *sefiros*: the voice of the *Aibershter* breaks down the trees. "Really it's almost a joke. What's the big deal?" The voice of the *Aibershter* can do a lot more than break a few trees. So what's the story? "If He would show you a voice that would break more than a few trees, you wouldn't be able to receive it." It would blow everything up.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.title: A voice that breaks a few trees
blocks.text: So He breaks a few trees and you're scared; He makes a few lightning flashes and everybody says, "Wow!" and starts praying, like by Yona, when the waves went up and down. But the power of the *Aibershter* is much greater, for sure.

blocks.text: So it is in all the *sefiros* except *tevuna*, whose whole matter is that he enclothes it down to the sheep. The main thing of *tevuna* is not the depth of the *chachma*, but that he brought it all the way out to the lowest level: and it is the same depth, "the same depth", the depth of the *chachma*. *Bina*, doing *hisbonenus*, catches the inner core of *Ima* and of *Abba* and understands it; then, through the vessel of *tevuna*, he brings that depth of *Abba* out to the sheep.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: So *tevuna* is not the depth of *chachma*: it is the shallowness of the sheep. That is its whole definition. However deep he understands it, he is just a *tafsan*; what makes him an *ish tevuna* is that he brought it out to the lowest level, and the lower the level, the bigger the *tevuna*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: So as *bina* from down to up is the biggest, *mamash* grasping the Essence, so is *tevuna*. All the other things, like the glory and splendor of the *Aibershter*: you can't have them as they are. They'd blow you away; not just us, the whole universe, all of *Atzilus*, *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, with *Adam Kadmon* and everything. So with *netzach*, *hod* and the rest. Except for *tevuna*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: What we're learning now, *mamash* this book, is the *tevuna* of the Essence, not enclothed. The *chachma* here is enclothed, in *mashal* after *mashal* after *mashal*; so is the *chesed*. We feel the *Aibershter* is doing us a *chesed*; if we really felt it, "we would start crying and laughing and rolling on the floor", and that is feeling just a little. "If you'd feel all the *chesed*, you'd stop existing."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: *Tevuna* is *davka* the opposite: a tiny little drop for a little, tiny sheep, *davka* to "lowlifes like us", not to the big shots. And the lower the sheep, the bigger the *tevuna*. That is *mamash* the matter of *tevuna*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: All the other *sefiros* come down with a *tzimtzum*: the *chesed*; the *gevura* (we get the fantastic *gevura* of the *Aibershter* here); the *tiferes*, the fantastic glory and splendor; and the *Malchus* coming down to us through this still comes with *tzimtzumim*. But this is the original *tevuna*, not a *tzimtzum* of it; just the opposite: on the 3,000th *mashal* is the biggest *tevuna*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: That's the original *tevuna*. What proves he's an *ish tevuna* is *davka* the last *mashal*, where it comes to the sheep. If he understands it all the way down but can't get it to the sheep, he is just a *chacham* or a *mevin*, not an *ish tevuna*. So this is literally the *tevuna* of the *Aibershter* Himself, of the *Ein Sof*, of the Essence.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: That's the other thing. "But you're just grasping an explanation: no comprehension of the *mahus*." Yes, but the explanation itself is the *tevuna* of the *Ein Sof*, and we grasp the actual explanation. "But that's not how He understands." No: this is not the *bina* of the *Ein Sof* but His *tevuna*, made to explain. This is Torah, the actual explanation the *Aibershter* came up with and gave us. Grasping it, you're *mamash* grasping the Essence. It's not like other things.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.title: An explanation of a hurricane
blocks.text: Grasping an explanation of an airplane is not grasping an airplane; an explanation of a hurricane is not *mamash* a hurricane. Here it is different. There, what you grasp is the *tevuna* of the explainer; and here that is exactly it: you grasp the *tevuna* of the explainer, literally, *lisvunaso ein cheker*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: And as we learned, upstairs there is no such thing as *tevuna*: the *tevuna* is the Essence, especially since this is not even the *tevuna* of *Yachid* but of the *Ein Sof*. As it explains, the whole *tzimtzum* was a descent of the SaG, *Malchus* of *tevuna*, and from *Malchus* of *tevuna* come the letters, the separate, external explanations. So we literally catch the *Malchus* of *tevuna* of the *Aibershter*, and *mamash* grasp it: right now it is going into our heads, so that we can think about it. Literally the *Aibershter* is going into our heads: *v'shachanti b'socham*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: This is bigger even than the Holy Ark, where the *Shechina* was *Malchus* of *Atzilus* enclothed in *Malchus* of *Beriya*. This is *Malchus* of *tevuna* of the Essence, higher than *Yachid*, not enclothed at all (even in *Yachid* nothing is really separate: *lav mikol ilein middos klal*). It is the actual intellect of the giver going into the receiver.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: That's why it is *davka* *bina*, for two things. From down to up it is the perfect vacuum cleaner, a total zero, not almost zero, *kula kamei k'la chashiv*, as by the others: a total *ayin*. From up to down it is the perfect opposite of a vacuum: the *tevuna* is *mamash* *ein od milvado*, "the actual Him."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: This is also *teshuva ila'a*: *v'hanefesh tashuv ad ha'Elokim*, not almost, all the way. So it is a very big thing about *bina*, about *hisbonenus*, about *Chassidus* in general and this book in particular: it is literally the *Aibershter* Himself, bigger than the Holy Ark.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: ("Wow.") Yes, that's exactly what it is. But the wow is *chachma*: wow means *hafla'a*. And you're not getting the full wow, "because if you would get the full wow, you'd explode." ("I'm getting the wow according to the *tevuna* of the *Aibershter*.") Yes, but the *chachma* is enclothed: "a *tzimtzum* of a wow." The *tevuna* itself is *mamash* the *tevuna* of the Essence.

blocks.text: Reb Hillel Paritcher explains this too, with a *mashal* for the whole beginning of the chain of *yesh* from *ayin*: it is *tevuna*. The *yesh* is *davka* in *tevuna*, more than in *bina*: *bina* is called a *yesh* in relation to *chachma*, while *tevuna* is the actual *yesh* of the receiver, unchanged the whole way down. His *mashal* is a teacher and a student: giving the student an explanation, through *tzimtzumim* fitted to the receiver, the teacher actually gives himself.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: The *tevuna* is the actual *tevuna*, not a *tzimtzum* of it; just the opposite. ("I never *chapped* that that's the *tevuna*.") Everything else is less of the Essence the more it goes down; by *tevuna* the more it goes down, the more *tevuna* there is, the more it is the *tevuna* of the *ish tevuna*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: Grasping part of the *etzem* is grasping the whole *etzem*. And this is the *tevuna* of the Essence: not even like *Yachid*, non-separate, but *mamash* the Essence, which has no parts. So it is *mamash* a grasp of the actual *etzem*. Learning *Chassidus*, learning this, you grasp an explanation, and it makes no difference: the explanation itself is the *etzem* of the *tevuna*. That is the whole chain of *yesh* from *ayin*, and it is *davka* by *Chassidus*, more than by any other part of Torah, which is only an enclothing.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 072 is a free discussion that reads no line; it sums up the whole chapter before chapter 7, so it is placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: There the whole thing is enclothing: what is explained is not the Essence. As the *Tanya* says, the *mitzva* and its reason are the *Aibershter*'s will and *chachma*: He wanted that if such and such a guy did this and another did that, the ruling should come out so. But it comes enclothed in a *davar zar*, something foreign, so it is not really the whole *chachma*.

blocks.title: Passing the salt
blocks.text: Your father, three people away at the table, asks for the salt. Your *chachma*: pass it to the guy next to you, he passes it on, and it reaches him. That is *mamash* your own *chachma*, but enclothed in a total *davar zar*, a big *tzimtzum*: you don't really get the whole *chachma* through it, "even though in a way you do." So in the Talmud you *mamash* *chap* the actual *chachma*, but through a *davar zar*: "if the donkey knocks over something, then this guy says that his donkey knocked over something, etc."

blocks.text: Here it is a whole different thing. First, the *tevuna* is the actual *tevuna*, not a *tzimtzum* of it: the more it goes down, the more it is the *tevuna*. Second, it is the *tevuna* of the thing itself, *shaashuei hamelech b'atzmuso*, the King's delight in Himself.

blocks.text: That also explains why now, *davka*, is the generation of *tevuna*: we're the lowest, and *tevuna* is *davka* in the lowest, by the sheep. "They're not even people; they're just sheep."
